transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-01 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Elmcrest Head of Data), Marcus Reynolds (CTO), Aisha Khan (Security Lead)

[00:00] Sofia: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Daniel and Priya with me. Quick round of intros?
[00:12] Laura: Hey all, Laura here, I'll own data integration and run the pilot on our side.
[00:17] Marcus: Marcus, CTO, I'm here for architecture and timelines.
[00:22] Aisha: Aisha, security lead, I'll be owning compliance questions.
[00:28] Sofia: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on success criteria, timelines, security, and next steps for Elmcrest's onboarding. We'll also confirm connectivity and whether you'll be on Hosted API or Dedicated / Private.
[01:02] Priya: Quick note, we typically recommend starting on Hosted to get samples and integration velocity, then move to Dedicated if you need throughput or isolation. But if you have strict data residency or VPC requirements we can stand up Private.
[01:25] Marcus: Our main constraint is data isolation and audit trails; we may need a VPC connect or a private deployment depending on what Aisha confirms. Latency isn't super strict but throughput for batch inference matters.
[01:44] Aisha: We require SOC2+ and everything encrypted at rest; we prefer customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). Also SSO via SAML, RBAC for roles, and audit logs retained 1 year. Do you support that out of the box?
[02:10] Daniel: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, long-term audit logs as an add-on, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS options. We'll send the SOC2 pack and architecture notes.
[02:34] Laura: Great, please send the SOC docs and the network diagram. Also we need to know firewall/IP ranges and whether NAT egress will be used for the private control plane.
[02:50] Priya: We'll include the network diagram and a list of IPs to allowlist. For Dedicated we can also provide peering options. Small caveat, sometimes our auto-transcribed docs call Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Dedict, sorry auto transcript.
[03:12] Sofia: No worries. Onboarding timeline idea: week 0 share keys and docs, week 1 integration and small test payloads, week 2 run benchmark and evaluate cost/latency, week 3 pilot full workload if all good. Thoughts?
[03:32] Marcus: That sounds fine. Our internal target is to go live with a pilot by March 10th, so your week 0 would be tomorrow basically.
[03:41] Sofia: We'll prioritize. We'll provision sandbox API keys and a small test Dedicated pool if you'd like to see isolation variants.
[03:52] Aisha: About encryption: we need to ensure KV cache doesn't leak PHI. Do you provide prefix/KV cache controls or disable cache per-tenant?
[04:08] Priya: Good question. We expose controls to disable KV prefix caching per workspace and also support encrypted caches in Private deployments. We'll document exact configurations.
[04:22] Laura: For model selection: are you recommending open models or Redwood-hosted balancer? We have concerns about hallucinations for clinical text.
[04:33] Priya: For clinical text, we typically start with curated open models we've validated — Redwood also has verified performance profiles. For safety-critical workloads we add evals on your prompt sets and we can suggest quantization profiles and fallback model routing. We'll run a quality baseline during the benchmark.
[04:58] Marcus: Any limitations on throughput for Dedicated? We expect bursts up to 200 concurrent requests during peak.
[05:10] Daniel: We can size Dedicated pools to meet SLOs; we'll need your RPS distribution, average seq length, and latency targets. Priya will send a sizing template.
[05:25] Sofia: On pricing, we'll give a pilot pricing sheet and committed Reserved capacity options when you go Dedicated. Also note that caching and batching will substantially reduce per-token cost.
[05:42] Aisha: Regarding compliance, can you provide attestation for data residency? We store EU patient data and need everything to stay in-region.
[05:55] Priya: Yes, we have region pinning and private control plane options for on-prem or VPC-deployed control planes; we'll include the compliance doc.
[06:08] Laura: Ok, action items recap?
[06:14] Sofia: I'll send onboarding packet with SOC2 & security pack, sandbox keys, and network IPs to allowlist. Priya will share benchmark template and schedule a tech deep dive. Daniel will follow up on pilot pricing. Customer to provide network contact, allowlist, and KMS preference.
[06:36] Marcus: One last question — competitor question — are there any migration helpers if we previously tested Anthropic or OpenAI endpoints?
[06:48] Priya: We have integration adapters and a migration doc; can translate prompts and some config but quality evals are necessary.
[06:58] Aisha: We'll need a short security review call with your security team next week.
[07:05] Sofia: Absolutely. We'll schedule that for early next week. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the pack and meeting notes.
[07:15] End of recording

Notes: transcript has typical auto-transcribe noise; names and product names may be slightly off in places. Links shared during the call: onboarding deck (link shared via email), SOC2 bundle (link), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).
